title: Yellow Butter Layer Cake with Chocolate Frosting
summary: A tender, buttery yellow layer cake built by the reverse-creaming method, sandwiched and covered with a rich, fluffy chocolate frosting.
equipment: two 20 cm round cake tins (5 cm deep), greased and base-lined
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: cake flour (or plain flour; see note)
ingredients.note: plain flour works with a slightly firmer crumb

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
dark chocolate (about 60-70% cocoa solids), melted and cooled
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat the Oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) for at least 20 minutes before baking, with a shelf set in the middle.

steps.title: Warm Everything Up
steps.text: Make sure the butter, milk, eggs and egg yolks are all at room temperature before you start. A reverse-creamed batter in particular needs everything at a similar temperature so it comes together smoothly rather than curdling.

steps.title: Reverse-Cream the Butter In
steps.text: Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt on low speed, then add the softened butter a cube at a time, mixing on low until it looks like damp sand. Coating the flour with fat before any liquid goes in limits how much gluten develops, which is what gives this cake its fine, tender crumb.

steps.title: Add the Wet Ingredients
steps.text: Whisk together the milk, eggs, egg yolks and vanilla. Add half to the dry mixture and beat on medium speed for 1 minute to build a little structure, then scrape down the bowl and add the rest in two more additions, mixing just until smooth each time.

steps.title: Divide and Bake
steps.text: Weigh the batter into the two tins so the layers rise evenly, level the tops, then bake for 28-34 minutes. Look for cakes that are golden, spring back when touched and are just pulling away from the sides, with a skewer coming out clean.

steps.title: Cool Completely
steps.text: Cool the cakes in their tins for 10 minutes, then turn out onto wire racks to cool fully before frosting. Frosting a warm cake will simply melt the butter in the icing, and it will slide straight off.

steps.title: Make the Chocolate Frosting
steps.text: Beat the butter on its own for 3 minutes until noticeably pale and fluffy. Beat in the icing sugar and cocoa powder on low speed, then add the cooled melted chocolate, milk, vanilla and salt, and beat for 2 minutes more until light and spreadable.

steps.title: Assemble the Cake
steps.text: Level the tops of the cooled cakes if they've domed. Sandwich the layers with a third of the frosting, spread a thin crumb coat over the top and sides, then chill for 15 minutes before covering with the remaining frosting and swirling it to finish.

tips: Mix the butter cubes fully into the flour before any liquid goes in - this reverse-creaming step is what keeps the crumb tender rather than tough.
Don't frost the cakes while they're even slightly warm; wait until they're completely cool or the frosting will slide off.
If the layers have domed, level them with a serrated knife before stacking for a neater, more even cake.
Chilling the crumb coat for 15 minutes before the final layer of frosting gives a much cleaner finish.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep the frosted cake covered at room temperature for up to 2 days, or in the fridge for up to 5 days, bringing slices back to room temperature before serving. Unfrosted sponges freeze well, wrapped tightly, for up to 2 months.
